name: Upflow anaerobic sludge blanket (UASB/EGSB)
principle: Follows the Paques BIOPAQ UASB licensor flow: wastewater is fed evenly at the bottom of a tall reactor and flows upward through a dense blanket of anaerobic granular sludge that converts COD to biogas; a three-phase (gas-liquid-solid) separator at the top retains granules, degasses the effluent and discharges treated water. EGSB adds higher upflow velocities and effluent recirculation for dilute streams.

process_steps.name: Biogas off-take
equipment: biogas line to desulphurisation and CHP

performance.basis: published UASB performance on industrial effluent

sources.note: Paques BIOPAQ UASB product pages, read 2026-11-13

costs.metric: UASB acquisition cost per organic load
costs.unit: USD per kg COD/d of design load
costs.basis: Derived from a Brazilian pulp-and-paper mill: UASB acquisition cost USD 3.4M against a design organic loading rate of 12,960 kg COD/d (9,288 m3/d wastewater). Acquisition cost only, single retrofit, no civils breakdown - an order-of-magnitude anchor, not a cost curve.

source.note: Ferreira et al., Biofuel Research Journal (2019): UASB acquisition cost USD 3.4M at 12,960 kg COD/d design load, Brazilian pulp mill, read 2026-11-16
